questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Personal connection to the destination (heritage / friends there/ etc.)

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Vibrant city, many oppertunities, easy to come to

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I didn't study at the university, but only had clinical interships. The Uni-life seems SO CHILL! But the clinical intershiplife is quiet intense, since they count on you to be there everyday 8-9 hours.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Difficult, I had the feeling I was the first outgoing to Berlin from my university (which I probably wasn't but it was very frustrating process both before and after)

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Introduktionmeeting with other erasmusstudents (good for socialising) other than that nothing (but I think if you're at the university you migth recieve more)

questions.answer: I spend most of the weekends in Berlin, but recommed Leipzig and Sächsische schweiz

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: yes

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Join AG's or do a Ultrasound course. If you have classes there is very good oppertunity

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: No

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Everything

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Be prepared that you will have long days at the clinic and also need to do A LOT of bloodsampling, since that is a doctors thing and they therefore use the students to do it. I felt quiet misused compared to DK, but I also learned things and it was very interesting to see the German healthcare (we are priviliged in DK:'))

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be a good germanspeaker! Or at least practice a lot before going since there is a little mercy in the hospital

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Feeling like a part of the team in my clinical intership. Learning how priviliged we are in DK

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Feeling misused in the clinicalship and not learning a lot compared t the hours I spend in the clinic (primarily due to having to do bloodsamples 4 hours a day)

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Overall super happy I did it (but am also native germanspeaker, imagine it being a different experience if german is at a low level)

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
